bib.title: Knowledge-Grounded Dialogue Generation with Pre-trained Language Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 3377-3390

question: How can a pre-trained language model (GPT-2) be used for document-grounded dialogue generation when the retrieved knowledge exceeds its input limit and no knowledge-selection labels exist?
hypothesis: A learned knowledge selector trained without human labels, jointly with GPT-2, beats truncation and label-dependent selectors.
contributions: A knowledge selection module for applying pre-trained language models to knowledge-grounded dialogue generation
An unsupervised approach that learns knowledge selection and fine-tunes the pre-trained model jointly
Empirical verification on benchmarks of knowledge-grounded dialogue generation

method.summary: KnowledGPT puts a BERT-based context-aware knowledge encoder and an LSTM sequential selector in front of GPT-2. The selector picks sentences one per step, up to Tmax, and GPT-2 generates from context plus the selected sentences. Training warms up on pseudo ground-truth built from the human response, then alternates a REINFORCE step for the selector (reward = unigram F1 of the GPT-2 response) and a curriculum step for GPT-2 that mixes pseudo and selected knowledge.

datasets.name: Wizard of Wikipedia
datasets.size: Train 166,787 utterances / 18,430 conversations; Valid 17,715 / 1,948; Test Seen 8,715 / 965; Test Unseen 8,782 / 968 (Table 7)
datasets.source: crowd-sourced on Amazon Mechanical Turk, Wikipedia as knowledge base (Dinan et al., 2019)
datasets.preprocessing: ParlAI code; only turns where knowledge is accessible are used; average 61.2 retrieved sentences and 1625.6 tokens of knowledge per context

datasets.name: CMU Document Grounded Conversations (CMU DoG)
datasets.split: official train/valid/test, version shared at github.com/lizekang/ITDD
datasets.source: crowd-sourced on Amazon Mechanical Turk, Wikipedia movie documents (Zhou et al., 2018b)
datasets.preprocessing: only turns where knowledge is accessible; maximum knowledge input length 502 tokens

models.name: KnowledGPT
models.architecture: BERT cross-encoder over (context, sentence) pairs, one-layer LSTM sequential selector with attention, GPT-2 decoder

models.name: GPT-2trunc
models.architecture: context and all knowledge concatenated, truncated to the GPT-2 limit

other.Wizard: ground truth randomly mixed with other candidates, repeated 8 times, mean and std reported

models.name: SKT+GPT-2
models.architecture: candidate selected by SKT fed to GPT-2

models.name: TMN, ITDD, SKT, DRD
models.architecture: Transformer Memory Network; Incremental Transformer with Deliberation Decoder; Sequential Knowledge Transformer (uses human knowledge labels, Wizard only); Disentangled Response Decoder (all parameters fine-tuned on full data)

models.name: DialoGPT
models.architecture: GPT-2 345M dialogue model, fine-tuned without knowledge

training.objective: Warm-up: MLE of selector on pseudo-knowledge D-bar and of GPT-2 on responses given D-bar, with D-bar chosen by Sim (unigram F1) against the response (Eq. 5). Joint: REINFORCE for the selector with reward R = Sim(generated, gold response) minus a mean baseline (Eq. 6); curriculum MLE for GPT-2 mixing D-bar and selected D' via Bernoulli(p) (Eq. 7).
training.lr: joint optimization: 5e-6 for selector g(U,D), 5e-5 for GPT-2; warm-up lr not stated
training.lr_schedule: halved if no improvement in PPL on validation set
training.steps: warm-up 1000; joint maximum step M not stated

other.curriculum p: p = p0 exp(-lambda m); p initially 1.0, anneals at rate 1e-5

inference.samples: one output per item; GPT-2trunc on Wizard averaged over 8 random knowledge orderings
inference.retrieval: knowledge sentences per context come from Wikipedia as supplied by the datasets (Wizard: retrieved from Wikipedia given last two turns and original topic); no retriever is trained here

parameters.selector stop: special embedding e_spe selected or Tmax reached

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: unigram F1 against the human response (ParlAI metrics.py)

metrics.name: BOW embedding Average/Extrema/Greedy
metrics.definition: embedding-based similarity (Liu et al., 2016) via nlg-eval

metrics.name: Human fluency, context coherence, knowledge relevance
metrics.definition: score in {0,1,2} per aspect, 300 examples each from Test Seen, Test Unseen, CMU DoG, 3 annotators, top-1 greedy; Fleiss' kappa

metrics.name: Knowledge selection accuracy
metrics.definition: accuracy of picking the ground-truth sentence (Wizard)

eval.protocol: t-test p<0.01 for bold improvements; 8 repeats for GPT-2trunc on Wizard; single run for the others (seeds not stated); human eval by 3 native speakers

availability.data: Wizard via ParlAI; CMU DoG via github.com/lizekang/ITDD

limits: Evidence is two small crowd-sourced datasets scored by word overlap against one human reply; only GPT-2 117M (and 345M) tested.
Forced-gold token-limit sweep (Table 9) is an oracle; the paper says one cannot locate the ground truth in practice.

Gains differ by dataset: on CMU DoG the response only weakly depends on the document (about 35% of conversations have BLEU < 0.1 to it), the pseudo ground-truth helps little, and KnowledGPT PPL is worse than GPT-2trunc.
Selection accuracy is low in absolute terms (28.0 and 25.4).
Seeds, hardware, compute, joint step count M, and curriculum constants p0 and lambda are not reported; code is not linked.
Retrieval itself is not studied; the knowledge sentences come with the datasets.
